question:
Who issued the silver rupee, which remained a standard coin for centuries after the ruler?

[CONSTABLE EXE 2023]
options: Babur
Sher Shah Suri
Humayun
Akbar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sher Shah Suri

Explanation:
Sher Shah Suri introduced the silver 'Rupiya' in 1540 CE, which became the standard coin in the Indian subcontinent for centuries. This coin weighed 178 grains (approx. 11.53 grams) of pure silver and was known for its high purity. Sher Shah implemented major monetary reforms, including a well-organized system of gold, silver, and copper coins. The rupee he introduced remained a key currency during the Mughal and British periods.

Extra Facts:
Sher Shah Suri not only reformed the currency but also contributed significantly to postal services, road construction (e.g., Grand Trunk Road), and administrative reforms. His reign was short (1540-1545), but his policies had a lasting impact.

question_hi:
चांदी की मुद्रा किसने जारी की, जो शासक के बाद सदियों तक एक मानक सिक्का बना रहा?

[CONSTABLE EXE 2023]
options_hi: बाबर
शेरशाह सूरी
हुमायूं
अकबर
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है शेरशाह सूरी

Explanation:
शेरशाह सूरी ने 1540 ईस्वी में चांदी की मुद्रा 'रुपया' जारी की, जो भारतीय उपमहाद्वीप में सदियों तक मानक सिक्के के रूप में प्रचलित रही। यह मुद्रा 178 ग्रेन (लगभग 11.53 ग्राम) चांदी की थी और इसकी शुद्धता उच्च स्तर की थी। शेरशाह ने अपने शासनकाल में मुद्रा सुधारों को लागू किया, जिसमें सोने, चांदी और तांबे के सिक्कों की एक सुव्यवस्थित प्रणाली शामिल थी। उसके द्वारा शुरू किया गया रुपया बाद में मुगल और ब्रिटिश काल में भी प्रमुख मुद्रा बना रहा।

Extra Facts:
शेरशाह सूरी ने न केवल मुद्रा सुधार किए, बल्कि डाक व्यवस्था, सड़क निर्माण (जैसे ग्रैंड ट्रंक रोड), और प्रशासनिक सुधारों में भी महत्वपूर्ण योगदान दिया। उसका शासनकाल छोटा (1540-1545) था, लेकिन उसकी नीतियों का प्रभाव लंबे समय तक रहा।

question:
Which of the following battles was fought between Babur and Rana Sanga in 1527?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Battle of Bayana
Battle of Khanwa
Second battle of Panipat
Battle of Chanderi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Battle of Khanwa

Explanation:
The Battle of Khanwa was fought on 17 March 1527 between Babur and Rana Sanga. This battle marked a turning point in the expansion of the Mughal Empire and the decline of Rajput power. Babur used the 'Tulghuma' and 'Rumi' warfare tactics, which led to his victory. Rana Sanga, the ruler of Mewar, led a large combined Rajput army but could not withstand Babur's forces. After this battle, Mughal dominance was established in North India.

Extra Facts:
Babur laid the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India and had earlier defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat (1526). Rana Sanga was considered the pride of the Rajputs and had won many battles before Khanwa. After this battle, Babur adopted the title 'Ghazi', meaning 'Destroyer of Infidels'.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा युद्ध 1527 में बाबर और राणा सांगा के बीच लड़ा गया था?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options_hi: बयाना का युद्ध
खानवा का युद्ध
पानीपत का द्वितीय युद्ध
चंदेरी का युद्ध
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है खानवा का युद्ध

Explanation:
खानवा का युद्ध 17 मार्च, 1527 को बाबर और राणा सांगा के बीच लड़ा गया था। यह युद्ध मुगल साम्राज्य के विस्तार और राजपूत शक्ति के पतन का एक महत्वपूर्ण मोड़ था। बाबर ने इस युद्ध में 'तुलगमा' और 'रुमी' युद्ध नीति का प्रयोग किया, जिससे उसकी जीत हुई। राणा सांगा, मेवाड़ के शासक थे और उन्होंने एक बड़ी संयुक्त राजपूत सेना का नेतृत्व किया, लेकिन वे बाबर के सामने टिक नहीं पाए। इस युद्ध के बाद मुगलों का उत्तर भारत में प्रभुत्व स्थापित हुआ।

Extra Facts:
बाबर ने भारत में मुगल साम्राज्य की नींव रखी और उसने पानीपत का प्रथम युद्ध (1526) में इब्राहिम लोदी को हराया था। राणा सांगा को राजपूतों का गौरव माना जाता था और उन्होंने कई युद्धों में विजय प्राप्त की थी। खानवा के युद्ध के बाद बाबर ने 'गाजी' की उपाधि धारण की, जिसका अर्थ है 'काफिरों का संहारक'।

question:
Sir Thomas came as an official ambassador from King James I of England to which Mughal emperor's court ?

[SSC CGL 2019]
options: Jahangir
Shah Jahan
Akbar
Aurengzeb
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jahangir

Explanation:
Sir Thomas Roe arrived at the court of the Mughal emperor Jahangir in 1615 CE as the official ambassador of King James I of England. His mission was to establish English trading rights in India. Jahangir granted him permission, and the English were allowed to set up a factory in Surat. This event marked the beginning of British influence in India. Thomas Roe spent three years at Jahangir's court and documented detailed accounts of the Mughal Empire in his travelogue.

Extra Facts:
The East India Company was established in 1600 CE, and Thomas Roe's visit followed this. Jahangir's reign (1605-1627) is known for the cultural and artistic development of the Mughal Empire. His wife, Nur Jahan, also played a significant role in politics. Thomas Roe's efforts secured trade privileges for the English in India, which later transformed into political dominance.

question_hi:
थॉमस रो इंग्लैंड के राजा किंग जेम्स प्रथम के आधिकारिक दूत के रूप में किस मुग़ल बादशाह के दरबार में आया था ?

[SSC CGL 2019]
options_hi: जहाँगीर
शाहजहाँ
अकबर
औरंगज़ेब
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है जहाँगीर

Explanation:
सर थॉमस रो इंग्लैंड के राजा किंग जेम्स प्रथम के आधिकारिक दूत के रूप में 1615 ईस्वी में मुगल बादशाह जहाँगीर के दरबार में आया था। उसका उद्देश्य भारत में अंग्रेजी व्यापारिक अधिकारों को स्थापित करना था। जहाँगीर ने उसे अनुमति दी और अंग्रेजों को सूरत में फैक्ट्री स्थापित करने का अधिकार मिला। यह घटना भारत में ब्रिटिश प्रभाव के विस्तार की शुरुआत मानी जाती है। थॉमस रो ने जहाँगीर के दरबार में तीन साल बिताए और उसने अपने यात्रा वृतांत में मुगल साम्राज्य की विस्तृत जानकारी दी है।

Extra Facts:
ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी की स्थापना 1600 ईस्वी में हुई थी और थॉमस रो का आगमन इसके बाद हुआ। जहाँगीर के शासनकाल (1605-1627) को मुगल साम्राज्य के सांस्कृतिक और कलात्मक विकास के लिए जाना जाता है। उसकी पत्नी नूरजहाँ ने भी राजनीति में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। थॉमस रो के प्रयासों से अंग्रेजों को भारत में व्यापारिक सुविधाएँ मिलीं, जो बाद में राजनीतिक प्रभुत्व में बदल गईं।

question:
The third battle of Panipat was fought in which of the following years ?

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: 1761
1707
1786
1751
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1761

Explanation:
The Third Battle of Panipat was fought on 14 January 1761 between the Maratha Empire and the Afghan ruler Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani Empire). This battle was one of the most devastating in Indian history, resulting in the defeat of the Marathas and a major blow to their power. The battle had far-reaching consequences on Indian politics, paving the way for the British East India Company to establish its dominance in India. Key figures like Sadashivrao Bhau and Vishwasrao (son of Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao) died in this battle.

Extra Facts:
Three major battles of Panipat are significant in Indian history:
1. 1526 - First Battle (Babur vs Ibrahim Lodi), establishment of the Mughal Empire.
2. 1556 - Second Battle (Akbar vs Hemu), restoration of Mughal power.
3. 1761 - Third Battle (Marathas vs Abdali), decline of Maratha power.

☛ Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao - Under his rule, the Maratha Empire reached its peak.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से किस वर्ष में पानीपत की तीसरी लड़ाई लड़ी गई थी ?

[SSC MTS 2023]

1786

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है 1761

Explanation:
पानीपत की तीसरी लड़ाई 14 जनवरी 1761 को मराठा साम्राज्य और अफगान शासक अहमद शाह अब्दाली (दुर्रानी साम्राज्य) के बीच लड़ी गई थी। यह लड़ाई भारतीय इतिहास की सबसे भीषण लड़ाइयों में से एक थी, जिसमें मराठों की हार हुई और उनकी शक्ति को गंभीर झटका लगा। इस युद्ध का भारतीय राजनीति पर दूरगामी प्रभाव पड़ा, जिससे ब्रिटिश ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी को भारत में अपनी सत्ता स्थापित करने का मौका मिला। सदाशिवराव भाऊ और विश्वासराव (पेशवा बालाजी बाजीराव के पुत्र) इस युद्ध में मारे गए थे।

Extra Facts:
पानीपत की तीन प्रमुख लड़ाइयाँ भारतीय इतिहास में महत्वपूर्ण हैं:
1. 1526 - पहली लड़ाई (बाबर vs इब्राहिम लोदी), मुगल साम्राज्य की स्थापना।
2. 1556 - दूसरी लड़ाई (अकबर vs हेमू), मुगल शक्ति की पुनर्स्थापना।
3. 1761 - तीसरी लड़ाई (मराठे vs अब्दाली), मराठा शक्ति का पतन।

question:
Who fought the war of Haldi Ghati against the Mughals?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Maharana Pratap
Rana Sanga
Raja Jaisingh
Rana Kumbha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Maharana Pratap

Explanation:
The Battle of Haldighati (1576) was fought between the Mughal Emperor Akbar and the ruler of Mewar, Maharana Pratap. The battle took place at Haldighati (near Gogunda) in Rajasthan. Akbar's army was led by Man Singh and Asaf Khan, while Maharana Pratap fought with his loyal chieftains and Bhil warriors. This battle is considered a 'symbol of Mewar's independence'. Although Mewar's forces had to retreat, Maharana Pratap never accepted Akbar's suzerainty.

Extra Facts:
Maharana Pratap was born on 9 May 1540 in Kumbhalgarh. He fought the battle with his famous horse, Chetak, which is legendary in Indian history. His resistance against the Mughals lasted for years, and he adopted guerilla warfare tactics from the forests. He died on 19 January 1597 but is remembered as a brave warrior and freedom-loving ruler.

question_hi:
मुगलों के विरुद्ध हल्दी घाटी का युद्ध किसने लड़ा था?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: महाराणा प्रताप
राणा सांगा
राजा जयसिंह
राणा कुंभा
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है महाराणा प्रताप

Explanation:
हल्दी घाटी का युद्ध (1576 ई.) मुगल सम्राट अकबर और मेवाड़ के शासक महाराणा प्रताप के बीच लड़ा गया था। यह युद्ध राजस्थान के हल्दी घाटी (गोगुंडा के पास) में हुआ था। अकबर की सेना का नेतृत्व मानसिंह और आसफ खाँ ने किया था, जबकि महाराणा प्रताप ने अपने वफादार सरदारों और भीलों के साथ मुगलों का सामना किया। इस युद्ध को 'मेवाड़ की स्वतंत्रता का प्रतीक' माना जाता है। हालांकि, युद्ध में मेवाड़ की सेना को पीछे हटना पड़ा, लेकिन महाराणा प्रताप ने कभी अकबर की अधीनता स्वीकार नहीं की।

Extra Facts:
महाराणा प्रताप का जन्म 9 मई, 1540 को कुंभलगढ़ में हुआ था। उन्होंने चेतक नामक घोड़े की सहायता से युद्ध लड़ा, जो इतिहास में प्रसिद्ध है। मुगलों के खिलाफ उनका संघर्ष लंबे समय तक चला और उन्होंने जंगलों में रहकर गुरिल्ला युद्ध की रणनीति अपनाई। उनकी मृत्यु 19 जनवरी, 1597 को हुई, लेकिन वे भारतीय इतिहास में एक वीर योद्धा और स्वतंत्रता प्रेमी के रूप में याद किए जाते हैं।

Explanation:

Extra Facts:

question:
Which Indian king issued a silver coin and termed it as Rupiya in the 16th century?

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options: Akbar
Krishnadevaraya
Hemu
Sher Shah Suri
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sher Shah Suri

Explanation:
In the 16th century, Sher Shah Suri (1540-1545 CE) issued a silver coin and named it the 'Rupiya'. This coin was a significant reform in the Indian monetary system. Sher Shah introduced several administrative and economic reforms during his reign, including currency reforms. He standardized the silver coin, which weighed approximately 11.534 grams. This coin is considered the precursor to the modern Indian Rupee.

Extra Facts:
Sher Shah Suri constructed the 'Grand Trunk Road' (G.T. Road), stretching from Kolkata to Peshawar. He also reformed the postal system and land revenue system. Though his reign was short-lived, his reforms influenced the Mughal Emperor Akbar's administration.

question:
Who was considered as the last powerful Mughal ruler of India ?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Akbar
Aurangzeb
Akbar II
Shahjahan
solution:

Explanation:
Aurangzeb (1658-1707 CE) is considered the last powerful Mughal ruler of India. He ruled for nearly 50 years and expanded the empire to its greatest territorial extent. His policies, such as the reimposition of the Jizya tax and destruction of Hindu temples, made him controversial. After his death, the Mughal Empire began to decline. Aurangzeb assumed the title 'Alamgir' and engaged in prolonged Deccan wars, which drained the empire’s resources.

Extra Facts:
Aurangzeb compiled the Fatawa-e-Alamgiri (Islamic law code). He built the Bibi Ka Maqbara (in Aurangabad, inspired by the Taj Mahal). His reign saw the rise of the Maratha power (under Shivaji). His religious orthodoxy led to the execution of the 9th Sikh Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur.

शाहजहाँ ने अपने शासनकाल (1628-1658) में कई भव्य इमारतों का निर्माण करवाया, जिनमें ताजमहल (आगरा), लाल किला (दिल्ली) और जामा मस्जिद (दिल्ली) प्रमुख हैं। उनके शासनकाल को मुगल वास्तुकला का 'स्वर्ण युग' माना जाता है। मोती मस्जिद के अलावा, उन्होंने दिल्ली के लाल किले में भी एक मोती मस्जिद बनवाई थी।

question:
The first battle of Panipat took place between Babur and _________.

[RRB NTPC CBT]

Sikandar Lodi
Ibrahim Lodi
Rana Sanga
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ibrahim Lodi

Explanation:
The First Battle of Panipat was fought on 21st April 1526 between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi (the last ruler of the Delhi Sultanate's Lodi dynasty). This battle marked a turning point in Indian history as it laid the foundation of the Mughal Empire. Babur used advanced artillery and the 'Tulghuma' warfare tactic to defeat Ibrahim Lodi, leading to the end of the Lodi dynasty. This battle established Mughal rule in India.

Extra Facts:
Babur described this battle in detail in his autobiography, 'Baburnama'. After the battle, he captured Delhi and Agra, declaring himself the Emperor of India. This war marked the beginning of the medieval era in India, with the Mughal Empire ruling for nearly 300 years.

question:
Who among the following was NOT one of the 'Nine Gems' of Emperor Akbar's court?

Osman Ali Khan

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Osman Ali Khan

Explanation:
Emperor Akbar's court had 'Nine Gems' (Navaratnas), who were experts in various fields. These included Abu'l-Fazl (historian), Raja Todar Mal (finance minister), and Fakir Aziao-Din (Sufi saint). Osman Ali Khan was not part of Akbar's court; he was the Nizam of Hyderabad, who lived much later (in the 20th century). Other members of Akbar's 'Nine Gems' were Birbal, Tansen, Man Singh, Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana, and Mulla Do-Piyaza.

Extra Facts:
Akbar's court was a hub of scholars, artists, and warriors. He promoted religious tolerance and even founded a new religion called 'Din-i-Ilahi'. Akbar strengthened Hindu-Muslim unity by marrying Rajput princesses. His reign is considered the 'Golden Age of the Mughal Empire'. The administrative and cultural reforms during his rule left a lasting impact on India.

question:
The Shalimar Gardens located in Lahore and Kashmir are architectures of the ____.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: British

Delhi Sultanate
Sikhs
solution:

Explanation:
The Shalimar Gardens in Lahore and Kashmir are prime examples of Mughal architecture. These gardens were commissioned by Emperor Jahangir and Shah Jahan during their reigns. Designed in the Persian style, they feature fountains, canals, and beautifully arranged flowerbeds. The Shalimar Bagh in Kashmir was built by Jahangir in 1619 CE, while the Shalimar Garden in Lahore was constructed by Shah Jahan in 1641-42 CE. These gardens reflect the Mughals' love for nature and artistic vision.

Extra Facts:
Mughal architecture is renowned for its Charbagh style (symmetrical gardens). The Shalimar Gardens are also designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Mughals built several gardens in India, such as Ram Bagh in Agra and the garden of Humayun’s Tomb in Delhi. These gardens symbolized both beauty and imperial power.

शालीमार गार्डन लाहौर और कश्मीर में स्थित मुगल वास्तुकला के उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण हैं। इन्हें मुगल बादशाह जहाँगीर और शाहजहाँ के शासनकाल में बनवाया गया था। ये उद्यान फारसी शैली में डिजाइन किए गए थे, जिसमें फव्वारे, नहरें और सुंदर फूलों की क्यारियाँ शामिल हैं। कश्मीर का शालीमार बाग 1619 ईस्वी में जहाँगीर ने बनवाया था, जबकि लाहौर का शालीमार गार्डन 1641-42 ईस्वी में शाहजहाँ ने बनवाया था। ये उद्यान मुगलों की प्रकृति प्रेम और कलात्मक दृष्टि को दर्शाते हैं।

To commemorate his victory over Gujarat, Akbar built ‘Gate of Magnificence’ the highest gateway of India of Fatehpur Sikri. What is another name for this gateway?

options: Gateway of India
Buland Darwaza

India Gate
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Buland Darwaza

Explanation:
Buland Darwaza was built by Akbar in 1575 CE to commemorate his victory over Gujarat. It is located in Fatehpur Sikri and is the highest gateway in India. Constructed using red sandstone and marble, this gate stands approximately 54 meters tall and is a masterpiece of Mughal architecture. Persian inscriptions on the gate reflect Akbar’s religious tolerance.

Extra Facts:
Fatehpur Sikri was established as Akbar’s capital but was abandoned due to water scarcity. The site is also famous for the dargah of Sufi saint Sheikh Salim Chishti. Verses from the Quran are inscribed on the Buland Darwaza, symbolizing the Mughal Empire’s religious harmony.

question:
Which architectural style of India was distinguished by the use of overhanging balconies and arched cornices?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Rajput
Sikh
Nagar
Mughal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rajput

Explanation:
The Rajput architectural style was distinguished by the use of 'overhanging balconies' and 'arched cornices'. This style primarily developed in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat. Rajput architecture also features lattice windows (jali), chhatris, turrets, and intricate carvings. Examples of this style can be seen in Chittorgarh, Hawa Mahal in Jaipur, and Jag Mandir in Udaipur. The style was influenced by Hindu and Jain architecture and used local materials like red sandstone and marble.

Extra Facts:
The Rajput architectural style prominently includes forts, palaces, and temples. It also incorporated stepwells (baolis) and reservoirs for water conservation. Rajput kingdoms like Mewar, Marwar, and Amber patronized this style. Despite later Mughal influence, the Rajput style retained its distinct identity.

In which the year was the second battle of Panipat fought between Akbar and Hemu?

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1556

Explanation:
The Second Battle of Panipat was fought on November 5, 1556, between the Mughal Emperor Akbar and the Hindu king Hem Chandra Vikramaditya (Hemu). This battle was a decisive conflict between the Mughal Empire and Hemu's forces. Hemu had captured Delhi and Agra but was defeated by the Mughal army in this battle, leading to his death. This victory helped the Mughals consolidate their power in India and marked the beginning of Akbar's reign.

Extra Facts:
The Second Battle of Panipat was part of the long struggle between the Mughals and Afghans. Hemu had won 22 battles and was a skilled commander. The Mughal army was led by Bairam Khan, as Akbar was only 13 years old at the time. After the battle, Akbar regained control of Delhi and Agra.

question:
The battle in which Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi was the:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Battle of Panipat
Battle of Chanderi
Battle of Chausa

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Battle of Panipat

Explanation:
The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire, and Ibrahim Lodi, the last ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. Babur's victory marked the beginning of Mughal rule in India. He used advanced military tactics like the 'Tulghuma' (flanking maneuver) and 'Rumi' (Ottoman-style artillery) to defeat Lodi's larger army. Ibrahim Lodi died in the battle, leading to the end of the Lodi dynasty.

Extra Facts:
After the Battle of Panipat, Babur captured Delhi and Agra, establishing Mughal dominance in North India. This battle shifted the political power balance in the region. Babur documented his victory in his memoir, 'Baburnama'.

question:
Who among the following was Akbar’s revenue minister?

[SSC MTS ]
options: Tansen
Todar Mal

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Todar Mal

Explanation:
Todar Mal was the chief revenue minister of Mughal Emperor Akbar. He implemented the 'Zabti System' or 'Dahsala System' (revenue assessment based on a 10-year average yield), which strengthened the economic stability of the Mughal Empire. This system was a revolutionary step to organize agricultural production and revenue collection. Todar Mal was considered one of Akbar's 'Navratnas' (Nine Jewels) and played a key role in administrative reforms.

Extra Facts:
Akbar's Navratnas included nine talented individuals like Todar Mal, Birbal, Tansen, Raja Man Singh, and Abul Fazl. Todar Mal's system became a model for later Mughal rulers. He also introduced 'Gaz-i-Ilahi' (a standardized measurement unit) for land surveys.

Explanation:
अब्दुल रहीम खान-ए-खाना बैरम खान का पुत्र था, जो मुगल सम्राट अकबर के दरबार में एक प्रमुख व्यक्ति था। उन्हें 'खान-ए-खाना' की उपाधि दी गई थी, जो एक उच्च सैन्य और प्रशासनिक पद था। रहीम एक कवि, विद्वान और सैन्य नेता भी थे, जिन्होंने अकबर के शासनकाल में महत्वपूर्ण योगदान दिया। उन्होंने बाबर की आत्मकथा 'बाबरनामा' का फारसी में अनुवाद किया और स्वयं भी कई दोहों और कविताओं की रचना की।

Extra Facts:
बैरम खान अकबर का संरक्षक था और उसने हुमायूँ की मृत्यु के बाद अकबर के शासनकाल की शुरुआत में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। हालाँकि, बाद में उसे अकबर द्वारा हटा दिया गया और उसकी हत्या कर दी गई। अब्दुल रहीम ने अपने पिता की मृत्यु के बाद भी मुगल दरबार में अपनी पहचान बनाई और अकबर के नवरत्नों में से एक बने।
